key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Gradual or sudden, often post-operative or bedridden. LOCATION: Focal or segmental lung areas. DURATION: Hours to days, can be persistent. CHARACTER: Mild dyspnea, chest discomfort. AGGRAVATING: Lying flat, shallow breathing. RELIEVING: Deep breathing, coughing, incentive spirometry, positioning. TIMING: Often worse in morning, improves with activity. SEVERITY: Mild to moderate (3-6/10). ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: Mild dyspnea, dry cough, chest discomfort, low-grade fever (if infection develops). KEY POSITIVES: Recent surgery, immobility, shallow breathing. KEY NEGATIVES: No severe dyspnea, no chest pain (unless severe), no wheezing.
